title: Customer action kit — inference queue oddities
body:
Purpose
This draft is a customer-facing advisory + verification kit for engineering contacts affected by the inference queue anomaly we observed on 2029-09-18. Target audience: product/platform engineers and integration leads who need concrete steps to validate service health, safely retry requests, and confirm data integrity after replay.

Short summary (one line)
Between 2029-09-18 03:12 UTC and 2029-09-18 07:04 UTC some tenants experienced duplicated tokens, truncated streaming sessions, and occasional out-of-order outputs when using long-context streaming or pinned KV-cache sessions. Most customers saw transient effects; a small subset with high-concurrency streaming experienced repeated partial outputs.

What customers may have observed
- Duplicate token fragments in streaming responses (e.g., repeated phrase blocks)
- Partial/stalled streams that resumed with older context (apparent misordering)
- Occasional 5xx errors for streaming endpoints followed by automatic reconnects
- In some replay attempts, clients saw slightly different completions versus the original response (root cause described below)

Immediate recommended customer actions (engineer checklist)
1) Validate current health (quick checks)
   - GET /v1/health (region) — expect 200 + {"queue_status":"ok"} within 1s.
   - GET /v1/usage/queued?tenant_id=<your-tenant-id> — confirm queued_backlog under typical baseline.
2) Safe-retry pattern (recommended)
   - Use idempotency keys for non-streaming generation calls; retry with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts.
   - For streaming sessions, avoid blind reconnects that drop the full context. Instead:
     a) If the stream stalled for <2s, allow client reconnect to resume using the original session_id.
     b) If you see duplicated tokens, treat as non-fatal and deduplicate on client when token sequences repeat (sample approach below).
3) Deduplication snippet (pseudocode)\   - keep last 32-token fingerprint per session_id; discard incoming tokens if fingerprint repeats consecutively.
4) Replay verification (how to confirm outputs match or diverge)
   - Re-run the same request with pinned model version and identical prompt + system messages.
   - Capture both full-token stream and chunk checksums (sha256) to compare with originals.
   - If replays differ in >2% of tokens for critical workflows, file a verification request to CS with the captured evidence.
5) Short-term mitigation knobs (on our platform)
   - If you rely on stream pinning, temporarily reduce max_concurrency to 1 for pinned sessions.
   - Toggle "aggressive-kv-eviction": false in your deployment profile to avoid premature eviction (we pushed default to false for affected tenants during mitigation).

What we fixed (customer-facing root cause summary)
- Root cause: a race condition in the queue-assembly layer interacting with KV-cache eviction during rapid autoscale events. Under specific timing, batches were assembled with stale batch-metadata leading to partial duplication or misordered assembly for affected streams.
- What we changed immediately: cluster-side hotfix to serialize batch-assembly with cache-eviction boundary checks; short-term throttle on autoscale bursts to stop co-located scale spikes.
- Longer term: a deterministic assembly rewrite and additional unit tests for multi-threaded cache eviction, scheduled for rollout in the next cadence.

Timeline (UTC)
- 2029-09-18 03:12 — anomalous increase in streaming retries detected by internal alerting (queue jitter metric).
- 2029-09-18 03:17 — first customer report (integration team) describing repeated partial outputs.
- 2029-09-18 03:45 — incident declared; SRE and runtime teams paged.
- 2029-09-18 04:20 — root cause hypothesis formed (queue-assembly + KV-eviction race).
- 2029-09-18 05:10 — mitigation deployed (serialization boundary + temporary autoscale throttle).
- 2029-09-18 06:05 — observable error rate for streaming dropped to baseline.
- 2029-09-18 07:04 — full removal of the temporary throttle after verification.

Impact and scope
- Affected: ~0.9% of active tenants during the window, mostly those with high concurrent streaming sessions and long context pinning.
- Customer-visible severity: intermittent duplication (majority cosmetic), small fraction saw functional degradation requiring replay.

Compensation and next steps for customers
- For customers who can demonstrate >5% of critical requests were materially affected (via checksums/replay evidence), CS will offer a targeted credit equal to one week of average usage for the impacted route. Please open a ticket with tagged evidence.
- We will follow up with a technical Q&A session for enterprise integrations on request (book via your account manager).

Guidance for customer success engineers (internal notes for replies)
- Keep messaging concise: we fixed the race; transient duplications are non-data-corrupting.
- Ask customers for three artifacts when requesting credit: original request id(s), token-stream capture, replay checksum.
- If a customer reports data-loss (very rare), escalate to eng-runtime and compliance immediately.
- Sample reply bullet points:
  * "We identified a race during autoscale that could cause duplicated fragments in streaming sessions. We deployed a hotfix that serializes batch assembly and restored normal behavior. If you capture the original request and a replay, we can validate and issue a credit if it meets the policy."

Open questions / things we still need to confirm
- Full list of tenants that experienced >1% mismatch on replays (WIP; eng producing list).
- Precise failure surface for a specific third-party client library that retries aggressively and may have amplified duplication.

Attachments / evidence to include with customer ticket (recommended)
- original-token-stream.txt (full tokens with timestamps)
- replay-token-stream.txt (full tokens with timestamps)
- token-stream-checksums.json (sha256 per 128-token window)
- timestamped logs with session_id and request_id

Notes to self (rough)
- Need a short FAQ snippet for status.redwood.ai entry (limit to 3 bullets + one line mitigation).
- Confirm whether we can programmatically surface per-tenant replay evidence via the audit API (Confluence says planned).
- Follow up with product to decide if default "aggressive-kv-eviction" should flip to false permanently for pinned sessions.

Representative curl examples (for engineers)
- Health check: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Capture streaming session: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{\"prompt\":\"<your-prompt>\",\"session_id\":\"abc123\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream

Contact and next updates
- Primary CS contact: asha.patel@redwood.ai
- Engineering follow-up channel: #ops-incident-4521 (will post timeline + artifact bundle)
- Expected next customer update: consolidation of per-tenant verification results within 72 hours.

-- end of draft --

(Informal fragments present intentionally — this is a working advisory, please edit for tone before sending externally.)
